data.long_meaning: In Sanskrit, Ravi comes from the word ‘Ravi’, which means ‘Sun God’. The name is derived from the god Ravi, who is considered the god of the sun in Hindu mythology. In Hindu culture, the sun is a symbol of energy, strength, and life, making Ravi a powerful and auspicious name for a baby boy.

vedic_reference.note: Ravi is a name derived from the Sanskrit word रवि (ravi), which means 'sun'. In Hindu mythology, Ravi is the name of the Sun God. It is also mentioned in various Vedic texts, such as the Rigveda and the Atharvaveda.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ravi holds immense significance in Hindu culture as it is the name of the revered Sun God. It is also a name of great importance in various Hindu literary works, including the epic Mahabharata, where Ravi is discussed as one of the mighty gods of the solar system and the celestial bodies that influence the rotation of the planets.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Ravi holds a position of immense importance as it represents the divine energy of the Sun. The Sun is considered the giver of life, and many spiritual practices involve facing the sun as a symbol of spiritual purification and enlightenment. Ravi, thus, carries the blessings of this powerful energy source, instilling a sense of positivity, wisdom, and vitality within those who bear the name.

historical_references.reference:
Ravi is derived from Sanskrit root 'Ras' meaning 'Juice', and was the name of the Sun God in the ancient Hindu civilization.
Time period: 2000 BCE - 500 CE.
Context: In Hindu mythology, Ravi is considered to be the brother of Devasani, the goddess of dawn, and together they form the first couple of the day. The Sun God is also referred to as 'Surya'.
